features.name: call_duration_log_norm
features.description: Log-transformed and normalized call duration, capturing diminishing returns of longer calls on a smooth scale suitable for linear margins
features.expected_model_benefit: Smooth continuous signal for call engagement intensity, avoids heavy-tail distortion in SVM kernel

features.name: economic_stress_index
features.description: Composite economic stress score combining employment variation rate and euribor rate, normalized to [0,1]. Higher values indicate more stressed economic conditions
features.expected_model_benefit: Linear projection of macro-economic environment onto a single axis useful for SVM hyperplane separation

features.name: prior_contact_success_score
features.description: Score reflecting prior campaign outcome quality: successful previous outcome (poutcome=1) with recent contact (low pdays) gets highest score
features.expected_model_benefit: Encodes prior campaign success signal as continuous score for linear decision boundary

features.name: campaign_contact_burden
features.description: Normalized measure of how many times a client was contacted in this campaign, log-scaled to penalize excessive contacts
features.expected_model_benefit: Captures diminishing returns and potential annoyance from repeated contacts as smooth linear feature

features.name: consumer_confidence_norm
features.description: Normalized consumer confidence index shifted to [0,1] range, where higher values indicate more positive consumer sentiment
features.expected_model_benefit: Direct linear signal of consumer sentiment for SVM margin optimization

features.name: age_financial_maturity_score
features.description: Smooth score capturing financial maturity by age, peaking around middle age (35-55) where financial product interest is typically highest
features.expected_model_benefit: Non-linear age effect linearized as a smooth score for SVM to exploit without polynomial features

features.name: debt_burden_composite
features.description: Composite debt burden score combining housing loan and personal loan indicators, weighted by severity
features.expected_model_benefit: Single continuous debt burden axis for linear separation of financially constrained vs free clients
features.formula: np.clip((np.where(housing == 1, 0.4, np.where(housing == 2, 0.0, 0.2)) + np.where(loan == 1, 0.4, np.where(loan == 2, 0.0, 0.2)) + np.where(default == 1, 0.2, np.where(default == 2, 0.0, 0.1))), 0.0, 1.0)

features.name: education_job_alignment_score
features.description: Normalized composite of education level and job category as proxy for socioeconomic standing, useful for linear projection
features.expected_model_benefit: Smooth socioeconomic proxy enabling linear SVM to capture education-job interaction without explicit cross terms

features.name: recency_previous_contact_score
features.description: Score for recency of previous campaign contact: 0 if never contacted (pdays=999), increasing as contact was more recent
features.expected_model_benefit: Continuous recency signal that linearizes the pdays spike at 999 for better SVM margin utilization

features.name: macro_employment_pressure
features.description: Normalized employment pressure combining nr.employed and emp.var.rate to capture labor market tightness as a single linear feature
features.expected_model_benefit: Reduces correlated macro features to single axis, improving linear SVM conditioning

features.name: contact_channel_recency_quality
features.description: Semantic assessment of contact quality combining channel type (cellular=1 vs telephone=0) and timing (month and day_of_week). Cellular contact in mid-week during spring/summer months scores highest as these tend to yield better engagement
features.expected_model_benefit: Encodes domain knowledge about optimal contact conditions as a smooth score for linear SVM

features.name: client_receptivity_composite
features.description: Weighted composite of signals indicating client receptivity: cellular contact, no default, previous success, and reasonable campaign count
features.expected_model_benefit: Single composite receptivity score that projects multiple weak signals onto one linear axis for SVM margin
